proposals.note: Ring-entangling block with Z3 cyclic symmetry (shift by 2). Six CNOTs form a closed ring for nearest-neighbor entanglement; six CRZs add a second entangling layer on the same ring to strengthen pairwise Z_iZ_j correlations needed by the 21-observable readout. Uniform RY with tied theta1 provides symmetric single-qubit rotation. The RZ layer splits into even/odd parameter groups (theta3/theta4), preserving invariance under the order-3 cyclic shift while granting two extra degrees of freedom beyond the fully-cyclic 3-param design. Total 24 gates, 4 trainable parameters—slightly more expressive than c0004 (5 params) but with a tighter symmetry constraint that should reduce variance on this 6-site regression task.

proposals.note: Dropped hypothesis after verifier showed label-preservation violated (59.6% of rows) and equivariance failed (residual 0.67). Targets are site-index-dependent, so no relabeling invariance is safe. Block uses 24 gates in a ring topology (CNOT+CRZ ring) with 4 tied parameters: t1/t2 alternate RY on even/odd sites to capture site-parity structure, t3 is a global RZ, t4 is a uniform CRZ coupling. Fewer parameters than c0001 (8) but more structured than c0004 (5 params, 21 gates). Ring CNOT gives full connectivity in 6 gates; CRZ ring adds parameterized entanglement aligned with the ZZ readout observables.

proposals.note: Ring-topology block: 6 CNOTs + 6 RZZ (replacing CRZ from c0005/c0006) + 6 RY + 6 RZ, all with tied params (3 total). RZZ chosen over CRZ because it directly generates Z_i Z_j correlations that the 21-observable readout (single Z_i and pairwise Z_iZ_j) can exploit without additional basis changes. Cyclic symmetry (0,1,2,3,4,5) preserved by uniform ring connectivity and tied parameters. Lower param count (3 vs 4) reduces overfitting risk while the RZZ entangler may align better with the diagonal-observable readout structure.

proposals.note: Builds on best performer c0006 (dev risk 0.0106). Same 24-gate CNOT/CRZ/RY/RZ skeleton with 4 tied params, but two changes: (1) split RY into two tied params (ry1 on even, ry2 on odd qubits) to break the bipartite symmetry and add expressivity for the two distinct targets; (2) replace the ring CRZ topology with a skip-one ring (distance-2 pairs) so that the 15 pairwise Z_iZ_j observables receive contributions from both nearest-neighbor (CNOT) and next-nearest-neighbor (CRZ) correlations. No hypothesis claimed since the best-scoring prior (c0006) used none and the verifier confirmed a trivial group adds no benefit.

proposals.note: Ring-entangling block with cyclic-by-1 symmetry. Order: RY -> CNOT ring -> RZ -> CRZ ring. Placing CNOT before RZ means the Z-rotation acts on already-entangled states, enriching pairwise ZZ correlations that the diagonal readout exploits. Three tied parameters (one per gate type) keep capacity low while the 24-gate ring gives full nearest-neighbor entanglement on all 6 sites. Hypothesis: invariance under cyclic site relabeling (1->2->...->6->1), matching the ring topology and uniform single-qubit layers. This mirrors the top-scoring c0006/c0008 structure (dev risk ~0.011) but adds the required verifiable symmetry claim.

proposals.note: Builds on the best-performing family (c0006/c0008, dev risk ~0.011) with 24 gates in a ring topology. Key change: split the 6 CRZ entangling gates into two tied groups (crz1 on even-indexed pairs, crz2 on odd-indexed pairs) to break the perfect translational symmetry. The verifier confirmed targets are NOT invariant under site relabeling (74.6% violation), so no hypothesis is claimed. The two-parameter CRZ structure lets the ansatz distinguish between two classes of nearest-neighbor couplings, which may help the linear readout separate alpha_0 from alpha_1. RZ and RY remain fully tied (rz, ry) to keep total parameter count at 4, matching the sweet spot observed in prior proposals. Ring CNOT topology ensures every qubit is entangled with two neighbors, giving good connectivity for the 21 pairwise observables.

proposals.note: Ring-topology block: 6 CNOTs form a closed ring (0-1-2-3-4-5-0), 6 CRZs on the same ring edges share one trainable angle, then uniform RY and RZ rotations on every qubit. Three tied parameters give a compact, expressive ansatz. The full cyclic shift (0 1 2 3 4 5) is an exact relabeling symmetry of the block: every gate maps to a gate of the same type with the same parameter, so the circuit is invariant under this Z6 action. This matches the ring-like indexing of the six measurement sites and should help the readout (Z_i, Z_iZ_j) capture periodic correlations. Compared to c0006 (4 params, no hypothesis) this trades one parameter for a verifiable symmetry constraint, reducing overfitting risk while keeping the proven CNOT+CRZ+RY+RZ ring structure that performed best in the prior pool.

Two distinct CRZ params (theta2 for edges 0-1-2-3, theta3 for edges 3-4-5-0) break the ring symmetry to allow asymmetric coupling, matching the top-performing no-hypothesis proposals. Dropped the prior hypothesis entirely since the verifier showed the task targets are NOT invariant under any site relabeling (74.6% violation rate) and the circuit failed equivariance. 24 gates, 4 tied params, low dev risk structure.
